idea.title: Tempus AI: can the data business carry the price?
idea.summary: Tempus AI has two businesses. Diagnostics, mostly tumour sequencing and Ambry's hereditary tests, brings in about three quarters of revenue and is paid per test. Data and applications, which licenses de-identified clinical and molecular data to drug developers and sells the company's own AI products, brings in about a quarter at a higher gross margin. The market prices the company as if the data business were already a proven engine. This idea tracks three questions over the next 12 to 18 months: whether Data and applications sustains its growth and proves to be a durable, high-margin business; whether the adjusted EBITDA margin turns up in 2027; and whether the company can fund itself, including the pending acquisition of Personalis, without issuing shares on dilutive terms.

evidence.title: Tempus AI voting control and executive performance shares (2026 Proxy Statement)

source.publisher: Tempus AI, Inc. (Schedule 14A Proxy Statement, SEC EDGAR)

claims.text: Class A shares carry one vote each and Class B shares carry 30 votes each; the two classes vote together.

As of the 27 March 2026 record date, Eric Lefkofsky, the founder and chief executive officer, beneficially owned 37,262,801 Class A shares (21.4% of the class) and all 5,043,789 Class B shares, giving him 57.9% of the combined voting power.

Long-term incentives for the named executive officers in 2025 were granted entirely as performance share units, tied to compound revenue growth and relative total shareholder return over 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027.

Each 2025 performance share unit award is split equally between compound revenue growth of at least 30% and total shareholder return at least 300 basis points above the Nasdaq Composite Index, measured over 12-, 24- and 36-month periods; earned units are capped at 100% of target.
Eric Lefkofsky's target award is 750,000 performance share units.

For the first 12-month period the compensation committee certified 82% compound revenue growth and 48% total shareholder return, about 29% above the Nasdaq Composite Index, so the first tranche (one third of target) was earned in full.

evidence.title: Tempus AI cash, debt, related-party revenue and Insights revenue at 30 June 2026

claims.text: Cash and cash equivalents were $599.6 million at 30 June 2026.
Marketable equity securities, all publicly traded common stock, were carried at fair value of $216.4 million at 30 June 2026.
The 0.75% convertible senior notes due 2030 have $750.0 million of principal and an initial conversion price of about $84.19 per Class A share.
The 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2032, issued on 12 May 2026, have $460.0 million of principal and an initial conversion price of about $69.26 per Class A share.

The convertible promissory note with Google LLC was carried at $187.9 million. It bears 6.0% interest compounded annually, matures on 31 December 2030, and its principal is reduced each year according to the company's use of Google Cloud Platform services.
In May 2026 the company repaid $307.7 million of principal under its additional term loan and revolving credit facility, and the credit agreement was terminated.
Insights revenue was $77.7 million in the second quarter of 2026, against $57.2 million a year earlier, and $149.0 million in the first half, against $106.7 million.
Revenue from related parties was $22.0 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $43.8 million in the first half, against $15.9 million and $16.5 million in the same periods of 2025.
The company's founder and chief executive officer is a co-founder and the executive chairman of Pathos AI, Inc., which the company reports as a related party.
On 24 July 2026 there were 175,390,967 Class A shares and 5,043,789 Class B shares outstanding.

evidence.title: Tempus AI second-quarter 2026 results and full-year 2026 guidance

source.publisher: Tempus AI, Inc. (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1, SEC EDGAR)

claims.text: Revenue in the second quarter of 2026 was $382.5 million, up 22% year over year.
Diagnostics revenue was $289.3 million, up 20% year over year: oncology test volume grew 31% and hereditary revenue grew 5%.
Data and applications revenue was $93.2 million, up 28% year over year; within it, Insights (data licensing) revenue grew 36%.
The company signed about $200 million of new Data and applications licences in the quarter.
GAAP gross margin in the quarter was 62.6% for Diagnostics, against 58.8% a year earlier.
GAAP gross margin in the quarter was 70.2% for Data and applications, against 72.7% a year earlier.
Loss from operations was $75.9 million, against $61.8 million in the second quarter of 2025.
Net income was $5.6 million, which included $98.5 million of unrealized gains on marketable securities and $55.6 million of stock compensation expense and related employer payroll taxes.
Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, was $8.0 million, against minus $5.6 million a year earlier.
Net cash used in operating activities in the first half of 2026 was $80.8 million.
Full-year 2026 guidance: revenue of $1.595 to $1.605 billion, about 25% growth, and adjusted EBITDA of about $65 million. The guidance assumes no impact from the Personalis acquisition.

evidence.title: CEO remarks on test pricing and data bookings, Morgan Stanley Global Healthcare Conference, 15 September 2026

source.publisher: Tempus AI, Inc. (Rule 425 filing, SEC EDGAR)

claims.text: Eric Lefkofsky said that, after the FDA approved the tumour-only version of the solid tumour assay, all of Tempus's solid tumour assays would run at ADLT pricing of $4,500 from the coming 1 January, that is, 2027.
He estimated that ADLT pricing for tumour-only tests adds about $80 million to $100 million of revenue and margin benefit.

He said Tempus expects approval and pricing of its liquid biopsy test in the second half of 2027, which would raise its price to the mid-to-high $7,000 range and add about $250 million to $300 million.
He said the data licensing business had about three consecutive quarters of more than $100 million of new total contract value, and about $200 million in the latest quarter.
He said Tempus had won a request for proposals from Merck and Moderna to be the national sequencing partner for the rollout of their V940 melanoma vaccine.

evidence.title: Terms, funding and expected timing of the Personalis acquisition

source.publisher: Tempus AI, Inc. (Form S-4/A, SEC EDGAR)

claims.text: Each Personalis share is to be exchanged for Tempus Class A stock. The exchange ratio is $16.25 divided by the Tempus stock price, and is fixed at 0.3356 when the Tempus stock price is $48.42 or less.

Tempus may elect to pay cash for up to 50% of the outstanding Personalis shares. It had not yet determined whether to do so, and would fund any cash payment through cash on hand, borrowing under existing or newly arranged credit facilities, and/or offerings of equity or equity-linked securities.
Personalis may terminate the merger agreement if the Tempus stock price determined at closing is below $46.00.

The companies expect the mergers to close in late 2026 or early 2027. The outside date is 20 April 2027, automatically extended to 20 October 2027 and then to 20 April 2028 if only the regulatory conditions remain unsatisfied.
The Tempus projections for Personalis show revenue of $115 million in 2027.
The Tempus projections for Personalis show adjusted EBITDA of minus $86 million in 2027, reaching zero in 2030, and unlevered free cash flow of minus $113 million in 2027.
